task: T-79 supporting measurement (not a task: no attempt owned)
question: The captain's T-79 row says a single stale auto-dispatch 'cannot discriminate between t36's route missed this one and the fix is inert in this process'. The repo's own T-21 instrument can discriminate: it compares each module's mtime with the live session's start.
answer: MEASURED: the fix is inert in this process. `lib/scheduler.js` — one of t36's two changed source files — was written at 02:34:15Z while the newest live session started at 02:10:11Z, so the running dsh holds PRE-fix bytes of the very module that composes the dispatch ticket. The terminal-task re-dispatch observed at ~03:09Z is therefore explained by the T-21 stale-module trap, not by a hole in t36's route.
session_start_relation: modules with mtime > the session start are RESTART-REQUIRED; modules older than it are FRESH (their on-disk bytes are the ones the process loaded, assuming they were unchanged at start).
affected_claim_classes: anything routed through lib/scheduler.js (dispatch / claim / kick / update paths)
lib/mpd-deltas.js (registry reads and --check inside the live process)
lib/tool-names.js (the read-only seat's advertised name list, T-49)
NOT_affected: t36's own evidence: its probe does `await import(pathToFileURL(join(root,'lib','scheduler.js')))` in a FRESH node process (raw/red-probe.mjs:77), which reads the current bytes from disk. So 'measured live' there means 'route exercised in a fresh process', and that result stands — including the refuted-acceptance-premise it records.
bound: This proves WHAT the live process is running. It does NOT prove t36's fix is correct in the running system: a restart (or a fresh-process probe, which t36 used) is what settles behaviour. The wave's bound therefore strengthens: no lane-B behaviour claim may rest on a live re-dispatch after the fix — and any live in-process reading of the four modules above is suspect until a restart.
